# 2696 at 6.58 (rank 1, Sun 02:42 UTC): identity, full behaviour, changes since 5.60, our gaps

Written Sun 22 Nov 2026, 03:20-04:10 UTC. Read-only and clean-room: the repository was cloned into
`scratchpad/intel2696/proj1` (no checkout of the default tree into anything of ours), candidate trees were extracted with
`git archive` into `scratchpad/intel2696/tree_*`, nothing was built or run, and no code, identifiers, comments or
constant tables were copied. Behaviour is described in our own words; numbers are given where they matter.
Predecessor: `notes/intel/top_2696.md` (5.60 study) and `notes/counters_2696_addendum.md`.

## 0. Headline

1. **2696 still plays shaunkar1/proj1.** Its 6.58 (board time 02:42:28) is most likely lot commit
   **`4392c25c2bd2b44b6e80ee6f39094c472c63bde4` (committed 02:19:04, lot tip until 02:44:32)**, or one of its five siblings pushed in the same
   17 s (02:18:48-02:19:04). The six differ only in one selector string; code and behaviour are otherwise identical.
   The only commit inside the usual 4-8 min lag is main `15098d8` (02:36), but it compiles in the plain base profile
   (no practice knobs) and cannot score 6.58. Same pattern as its 5.94 (16:17 Sat): lot batch 16:00, score 17 min later.
   No evidence of any other repository.
2. **The 6.58 is not a better fighter. It is a per-slot mixture of near-identical bots tuned on the fixed practice
   set.** At match start the bot hashes the hello seed and slot into one of 16 buckets and loads, for that bucket, one
   of 25 sub-profiles. Most of the 25 differ from the reference only in a random-number salt, a tiny movement jitter
   (pure re-rolls) and/or the attack health gate (35% or 45%); seven change one other practice knob (opening 60 / 100 s,
   "never start a fight", attack radius 160 m, retreat 20%, cube cap 5, drops off). In the 6.58 table only five of
   them are used: 9 buckets 35%-gate reference (2 of them with jitter), 3 buckets 45%-gate salts, 4 buckets
   "never start a fight". Because the
   hello seed is fixed per slot and practice matches are deterministic, each of the 48 matches always lands in the same
   bucket, so the team could search, bucket by bucket, for the variant that happens to score best on those exact
   matches (Walsh/Hadamard-style masks at 19:06 Sat, then greedy group swaps of 4 buckets every 10-40 min). Between the
   5.94 build and the 6.58 build **nothing that changes practice play was added except this mixture**. It is worth
   +31 kills on the fixed seeds and roughly nothing on new seeds (the final).
3. **The real bot (the reference sub-profile) is the 5.60 code family plus four practice changes**: attack on sight
   out to 220 m above 35-45% health instead of the fixed 170 m kite; grab near lasers and cubes even mid-fight; finish
   the spawn look before shooting crates; and, the most interesting one, **run to any supply drop (full repair + 3
   cubes) as soon as it is below full health, with priority over fighting**.
4. **New timing tricks:** the final is detected by the wall clock (any match after 16:02 UTC today plays the
   free-for-all posture from tick 0) and by a long hello-to-first-observation gap (over 400 ms). During the spawn
   turn the torso pitch encodes these timings and a config fingerprint, readable in recorded replays (a side
   channel used to calibrate the detector). Earlier pins were "probes" that stop playing on a condition (time, kill
   count against slot number, seed range, tick speed) so that the practice score itself reports facts about the
   scorer.
5. **README now carries an ownership and no-reuse notice** (added 02:04-02:15 UTC Sun, right before this batch):
   it says the repository is team TigerTown27's entry, all rights reserved, no copying or reuse of code,
   parameters or ideas, cites "excessive code reuse may result in disqualification" and threatens to report reuse
   (it also contains text aimed at other teams' AI tools [passage omitted]). For the owner's decision: our own log
   (`notes/submissions.md`, 02:40 UTC) records the organiser clarification "only exact code copies matter;
   recreating logic in our own optimized code is fine"; our rules audit (C15) keeps "ideas only, no code, no
   constants copied". This report gives numbers for understanding; engineers should choose and tune their own.
   Side fact: if TigerTown27 and 2696 are different teams submitting the same commits, the event rule "a submission
   with the same repository, commit or archive as another team's is disqualified, the later one" puts one of them at
   risk at verification.
6. **Biggest levers for us (section 6):** (1) the per-slot mixture itself (the only thing that explains 5.94 -> 6.58;
   expected +0.3 to +0.8 for us, practice only, costs 16-40 submissions on frozen code, and is gaming the fixed
   practice set, so the owner should decide); (2) supply drop as a second life (we never leave a fight for a drop);
   (3) a clock-based final switch, which would let every practice-only change be made without touching the final.

## 2. What the 6.58 build is

- One Go program: about 5,300 lines of pilot code in the binary (decisions 2,300, perception and timing 1,000,
  movement 700, aiming 370, profiles 460, I/O 230, the rest small) plus about 1,400 lines of map, navigation and
  protocol code. All comments were stripped from the repository on Sat evening.
  The simulator, lab tools and the variant file are not used by the submitted binary.
- A **base parameter set** (the same for practice and final), then a **profile string** applied on top. The profile
  string of this build is a mixture: header "16 buckets" + a 16-character table + 25 sub-profiles.
- **Bucket choice:** a 64-bit integer hash of (hello seed, slot), modulo 16. Rules (our audit L11): the hello seed is
  fixed per slot, so in effect the bucket is a function of the slot; the 48 practice matches are fixed, so each
  always uses the same sub-profile. In this build's table: 7 buckets run the reference, 4 run "never start a fight
  for the whole match" (opening gate of 600 s / 99 cubes), 2 run the reference with movement jitter 1, 2 run salt 6
  without the 35% gate, 1 runs salt 1 without the 35% gate.
- **Reference sub-profile** (what we should think of as "the bot"): attack-on-sight profile with 10-cube / 75 s
  opening, attack radius 220 m, grab on, spawn-look on, supply drops whenever below 100%, RNG salt 3, attack health
  gate 35%, plus the two final detectors (clock and ready gap).
- Re-roll knobs: an RNG salt (changes cover sampling, strafe timing, unstick directions, roam points) and a movement
  jitter (each move vector rotated by a pseudo-random angle of up to 1 degree keyed on seed, tick and slot; never in
  a known free-for-all). Both change nothing on average and everything per match.
- Sub-profile knobs present in the 25-entry list: opening length 60 / 75 / 100 / 600 s, opening cube cap 5 / 10 /
  99, attack radius 160 / 220 m, attack health 35 / 45%, retreat 20 / 35%, drop rule on / off, jitter 0-4, salts
  1-12. The six pins of the batch differ only in which entries the 16-bucket table uses (the five siblings each try
  "opening 100 s", "opening 60 s" or "never start a fight" on one of two groups of 4 buckets).

## 3. Behaviour in the squad (practice) posture

Throughout, "practice" means its own detector: nobody died that it did not kill, match time above 20 s, and no final
signal (section 3.2). The first 20 s of every practice match therefore run a third, "not sure yet" posture.

### 3.1 Start-up and map use

- Loads the mounted map (falls back to an embedded copy of arena v2), sets the arena margin (30 m default), builds a
  2 m walk grid: 3 m clearance, 9.5 m body, 1.2 m step-up, slopes up to 48 degrees; extra path cost 1.6 / 0.6 / 0.2
  for cells 1 / 2 / 3 cells from a wall; an "openness" field (distance to the nearest structure at least 8 m tall);
  connected regions with the largest one as "main ground"; for every roof or island region the cheapest jet-hop
  back to main ground (energy = jet drain x (climb / 8.5 + distance / 9 x 0.7) + 6, capped at 82).
- Weighted A* (heuristic x1.25, 30,000 expansions), replanned at most every 0.25-0.8 s; walks to the farthest path
  point within 26 m that is straight-walkable.
- I/O: decisions run on a worker with a 34 ms budget; a late or crashed decision is answered with the previous
  move/aim; queued observations are skipped to the newest one.
- At hello it also fingerprints every config section against the kit's config and starts a stopwatch from "ready".

### 3.2 Posture detection (and why it matters)

- **Final certain from tick 0** if the wall clock is after 22 Nov 16:02 UTC (2 min after the cutoff, valid 40 days)
  or if the time from its ready message to the first observation exceeds 400 ms (checked in the first 2 s).
- **Final certain later** if another mech dies (not its kill) before 40 s; any foreign death at any time ends the
  practice posture.
- Otherwise: 0-20 s "unsure" posture, then practice.
- Consequence: the team can tune practice behaviour freely; the final is protected by the clock, not by inference.

### 3.3 Perception

Vision (server list only; it does not model the cone except for an exploration map):
- Line of fire from its muzzle to the target's centre, then to its top (aim 0.6 m lower than the top), then to points
  0.75 radius left and right; a partial line sets a tight aim point and tighter fire tolerances.
- **Hostility:** a mech with a line on it whose torso points within max(6.9 degrees, the angle of 6 m at that range)
  of it, inside 260 m, gains 0.1 per decision (+0.3 more while charging a laser) and loses 0.05 otherwise; at 0.6
  (about 0.6 s of steady aim, 0.2 s while charging) it is hostile for 8 s. Within 30 m with a line: hostile 4 s.
  Damaged us: hostile 25 s.
- "Busy" mark: a mech that lost more than 20 hp in one decision without our hit, or charges a laser more than 0.6 rad
  off us (used only by final rules).
- **Unseen attacker:** a damage event from a mech not in view creates a ghost along the bearing, at the last known
  range if seen within 8 s, else 110 m (35 m for lightning, 60 m for mortar), or at a visible beam's origin; weapon
  learned from the event.
- Gun hit-rate learning per target (hits/shots after 6 shots).
- Motion model choice per target: five predictors (current velocity, 0.5 s average, 1.0 s average, standing still,
  half velocity) are replayed over its recent history at the bullet's flight time and scored; the best one (0.08
  hysteresis) is used for leading.
Sound:
- Near-band step, boost, jet, reload, laser-charge, lightning or gun sounds: torso turns to that bearing for 1.5 s
  (when nothing else claims the torso).
- Mech sounds become estimated noise points (near band at 0.6 of the near distance, mid band at the band middle,
  far band beyond), kept 20 s: used only in final-posture avoidance. Death sounds become death sites (final only).
Memory:
- Mechs kept 25 s (positions frozen at last sight), drones 6 s as tracks and 120 s as "drone homes"; cubes 40 s;
  crates and pickups until their spot is in near range, visible and empty.
- Damage time, bearing and a decaying damage total per attacker.

### 3.4 When it starts and when it avoids fights (practice timeline)

| Phase | Who is a legal target |
|---|---|
| 0-20 s (unsure posture) | only mechs marked hostile (aim 0.6 s, inside 30 m, or damaged it); "boss" mechs rated over 1.5x its strength are avoided (inside 150 m, or any distance with a line); "peer" mechs rated 0.85-1.5x are avoided inside 60 m with a line |
| 20 s until 10 cubes or 75 s (12 buckets; the whole match in the 4 "never start a fight" buckets; siblings tried 60 and 100 s) | only a mech that damaged it in the last 4 s from inside 100 m. The early practice hunter shooting from 100-150 m is not shot back; it keeps farming above 70% and hides below |
| after the opening | any mech inside 220 m while its own health is above 35% (9 buckets) or 45% (3 buckets); plus a mech under 40% inside 150 m while it is above 60%; walks toward any mech seen in the last 20 s while above 80% (worth up to about 90 m of walking) |

Fight-or-not on the chosen target, evaluated at its preferred range (if within 60 m of it or closing):
- fight if its time to kill the target is shorter than the target group's time to kill it (all hostile mechs with a
  line add their damage), or its modelled damage advantage exceeds 25 per second;
- with two or more hostile shooters and a kill more than 2.5 s away it needs a 1.5x time margin;
- "finishing" (kill under 1.6 s away) overrides every retreat and avoidance.
- Not fighting while being shot means "retreat to cover" (it still shoots back at legal targets on the way).
Its own model, house gun + laser mech, both at 0 cubes: at 100 m it rates itself 209/s against 141/s incoming:
kill in 6.7 s, death in 9.9 s, so it duels one hunter; with two shooting at 100 m incoming is 282/s (5.0 s), so it
disengages unless the kill is within 2.5 s. With only a gun against gun + laser (kill 18 s, death 9.9 s) it never
chooses to fight; it only returns fire while moving to cover.

### 3.5 Target choice

Among legal mechs seen in the last 0.3 s: score = -(target hp) - 2.5 per metre + 400 with a line + 350 if it hit us
in the last 4 s + 150 for the current target. The shot itself goes to the best legal mech with a line:
-0.6 x hp - 2 per metre + 200 for the target + 150 if it hit us in the last 3 s. A drone that hit us in the last 3 s
takes the torso, the gun and a held laser charge whenever no mech is shootable ("biter" rule).

### 3.6 Ranges and kiting

- No fixed range any more (the 5.60 build held 170 m). Preferred range = the best of 28 / 40 / 55 / 75 / 100 / 130 /
  160 / 190 m by "own damage minus 1.15 x incoming damage" (a closer step wins unless the farther one is 2 better).
  Its model: enemy gun hit chance 90% at 40 m falling 1.25 points per metre to a 6% floor (so the house gun is worth
  almost nothing past 110 m); own gun 97% at 40 m falling 0.35 points per metre (floor 30%), corrected by its
  measured hit rate; lasers flat to 280 m; lightning 230/s inside about 49 m.
- Resulting holds: about **100 m** against gun or gun + laser hunters (whatever it holds), **55 m** against laser +
  lightning, **28 m** when it holds lightning (rushes in with boost when more than 12 m outside a hold under 50 m,
  under 120 m away, energy above 45).
- Range is a soft term in the step scorer (1.2 points per metre off the hold, against a strafe bonus of up to about
  11), so it drifts within about 10 m.
- Boosts back when the target is more than 25 m inside the hold and energy is above 30.
- Target out of sight: walks to its last position until within max(8 m, 0.6 of the hold) (60 m at a 100 m hold).
- Never closer than 54 m to a lightning carrier unless it holds lightning itself (7 points per metre penalty), and
  dislikes any mech inside 60 m (1.5 per metre) unless its hold is under 60 m; 10 per metre inside 7 m.

### 3.7 Aiming, leading and weapon choice

- **Gun:** three-pass lead with the chosen predictor, 0.06 s latency, ballistic drop for jumping targets; fires when
  the next tick's turn-limited aim is within the body tolerances (yaw: angle of 0.85 x radius; pitch: 0.42 x height;
  0.22 / 0.12 when only part of the body shows) and the line to the predicted point is clear.
- **Laser:** starts a charge whenever off cooldown, in range (275 m) and the target is visible or seen within 1 s;
  not while a lightning carrier closes faster than 4 m/s at 46-68 m. Releases at full charge (or when the partial
  charge already kills), aimed at the highest clear body point (85 / 68 / 30 / 12% of height). Otherwise keeps a
  charge held when nothing is shootable. Laser on drones only above 150 hp; on crates only when no mech was seen for
  4 s and the crate has more than 100 hp. **No laser timing caution in practice** (no peeking, no hiding from
  charging lasers).
- **Lightning:** fires inside range - 1 m and within 90% of the cone; on drones only above 55% energy; on crates only
  above 70% energy.
- **Mortar:** never picked up (rank 0). The solver exists (ballistic, splash-safe, short flights) but is dead in
  practice.
- **Loadout:** never drops the gun; second slot laser (rank 3) over lightning (2.6); swaps lightning for a laser
  when one is within 3.6 m, never while its laser is charging.
- **Reload:** when nothing is in view and the magazine is at or under a third; after 1.5 s quiet and no mechs at
  two-thirds; after 6 s quiet whenever not full (not while farming).

### 3.8 Movement and dodging

- Every decision scores 49 candidate steps (standing, 16 directions x 2.5 / 5 / 11 m, plus the path's next point):
  goal distance, wall cost, zone (heavy penalty for being outside in 1 s, lighter for 4 s), exposure to each threat
  (its modelled damage x a hostility weight of 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 for bosses), +own damage for steps with a line
  to the target, the range term, strafe bonus, momentum (+1.2 for continuing), dodge penalties.
- Strafe side flips every 0.35-0.9 s (70% of the time).
- **Bullet dodge:** projectiles up to 260 m ahead and 14 m to the side (up to 14), mortar shells simulated to impact;
  simulates 1.0 s of its own movement with acceleration limits in three legs (0.1 s, 0.15 s, 0.75 s) over 17 x 9 x 9
  direction choices; a hit costs 100, a near miss up to 14, a shell splash up to 170; the cheapest first-leg direction
  wins the dodge term.
- Boost: zone (energy over 8), drop and grab (over 8), unseen sniper (over 10), retreat under fire (over 12), long
  trips over 40 m with energy over 75; never in the air except to unstick.
- Stuck 0.5 s: blocks the cells for 20 s, jumps and boosts in a random or goal-biased direction for 0.9 s.
- Off main ground (roofs): picks the cheapest hop and jets over.

### 3.9 Cover

- Safe-spot search: 48 random points 8-78 m away on main ground, inside the zone 12 s ahead; score = -path length,
  -150 x weight for every threat that sees the body (two heights and both shoulders), +0.5 x weight per metre from
  each threat (up to 120 m), -100 within 30 m of a threat. Kept for 2.5 s while still hidden.
- If still exposed to the two nearest hostiles: rings at 55 / 85 / 115 / 145 m, 16 points each, not closer to the
  main threat than 80% of the current distance; such a "far cover" is kept 6 s and travelled with priority and boost.
- Used by retreat, unseen-sniper evasion, boss/peer avoidance and healing.

### 3.10 Loot: crates, cubes, drones, weapons, stealing

Objective value minus 1.3 per metre in practice (0.6 in the final), +15 for keeping the last objective:

| Item | Value | Walk limit in practice | Conditions |
|---|---|---|---|
| cube | 110 | ~85 m | none (roof cubes only at its level) |
| crate | 105 | ~80 m | own health above 45% |
| drone | 170 (remembered home 155) | ~130 m | above 60%, no mech in view |
| weapon it wants | 70 + 45 x gain (200 + 30 x gain with an empty slot) | ~60-150 m | roof weapons cost 2.5 per metre of height + 25 and need jet energy; blocked with mechs near or under 60% |
| laser (when it has none) | at least 270 | ~208 m | |
| supply drop (as objective) | 170 (60 if held by another) | ~130 m | reachable within 25 s of landing |
| hunt a seen mech | 120 - 3 per second of age | ~90 m | above 80%, after the opening |

- Crates: stops at least 14 m away (farther if its gun cannot depress that far), backs off if closer, shoots with the
  gun; gives up after 14 s (ignored 90 s). Opportunistic crate shots at any crate within 50 m (110 m if no mech seen
  for 4 s) when nothing else is shot.
- Drones: approaches to 22 m and strafes; shoots drones within 60 m above 50% health and any drone that hit it.
- Cubes: gives up after 1.2 s within 2.8 m or 6 s + 1 s per 8 m (ignored 60 s).
- **Grab (new since 5.60):** a laser within 45 m, another wanted weapon within 25 m (only with an empty slot), or a
  cube within 18 m, path not longer than 1.4-1.5x, no mech within 30 m (cube: 25 m) of the item, own health above
  30%: it runs (with boost) and takes it, **with priority over fighting, retreating and avoiding**; 6 s timeout.
- While retreating calmly it picks cubes within 28 m. Kill cubes are just cubes (grab / objective). No explicit
  stealing of crates others shoot; in the final it walks to death sites (section 4).

### 3.11 Upgrade order

Plating, armour, laser damage, laser charge, repair nanites, gun damage, gun rate, lightning efficiency, servos,
lightning chain, capacitor, reactor, gyros, gun magazine, lightning range, then mortar items, gun velocity, sensors,
jets, laser pierce. (Ours puts nanites third.)

### 3.12 Healing, retreat, regeneration

- Retreat latch: under 35% (all buckets of this build; a 20% variant is in the list but unused) while being hit (or
  hit in the last 3 s), unless finishing; ends above 80%, or above 55% with no mech in view and no hit for 6 s.
- Also "retreat" without the latch when it does not want the fight but is under fire (2.5 s) or has incoming.
- **Holds fire while latched and not under fire** (lets regeneration start: 5 s delay, 45 hp/s; nanites 3.5 s and
  72 hp/s), boosts out under fire with energy over 12.
- "Hurt" (under 70%, hit in the last 40 s, a threat listed): only loot within 35 m, otherwise sits at a safe spot.
- About 19 s from 35% to 80% with base regeneration.

### 3.13 Supply drops (new since 5.60; probably its best real idea)

Config: called at 70 / 140 / 210 s, land 25 s later (95 / 165 / 235 s), 8 m ring, 4 s capture, **3 cubes and a full
repair**. Practice rule: **whenever its health is below 100%**, it takes the nearest drop within 200 m (straight
line) that is inside the next zone and that has landed or will land no more than 3 s after it arrives. Drop mode is
second only to an urgent zone move: above grab, unseen-sniper evasion, avoidance, retreat and fighting. It walks or
boosts (energy over 8, more than 12 m away), stops within 2 m, keeps aiming and shooting its target, and stays.
There is no contest check and no health margin in practice. Kept in every reference profile since Sat 11:27; a
larger radius (350 m) was tried at 12:19 and not kept.

### 3.14 Zone

Target circle = the end of the current shrink; aims to be inside by min(14 m, 0.35 r). Leave-by time = the earlier of
(the edge reaching it - 5 s) and (shrink end - path time x 1.1 - 3 s - 6 s). Late or edge within 3 m in 6 s:
urgent mode, boost, no strafing, still shooting. Not urgent: drifts toward the zone while fighting (low weight),
walks in with boost when more than 60 m out and energy over 60 when nothing else is wanted. Loot that will be outside
at arrival + 3 s is skipped; path cells outside the zone 4 s ahead cost extra.

### 3.15 Last stand

No dedicated rule. "Finishing" (kill under 1.6 s away) suppresses retreat and avoidance. With two left, all
avoidance switches off and it duels on its fight test. In the final shrink it obeys the urgent zone rule.

### 3.16 Timing tricks and probing

- Clock final switch (16:02 UTC today) and ready-gap final switch (over 400 ms), section 3.2.
- **Pitch side channel:** during the 1.7 s spawn turn, if the config matches the kit's, the torso pitch is set to a
  log-scale code of the ready gap (0.3-0.6 s), the median tick-pair wall time (0.85-1.15 s) and its minimum
  (1.15-1.42 s), in 0.03 rad steps; if the config differs, the pitch shows which section differs first and how many.
  Any public recording of its matches tells the team how fast and how "different" that environment is.
- Probe pins (Sat 09:19-17:23, not in this build): bots that freeze when kills reach the slot number (or 15 minus it),
  when the seed is below 1e6 or above 2^31, at a fixed match time, or when ticks run slower than a threshold: the
  resulting practice score reveals slot use, seed ranges and the scorer's speed.
- Per-slot mixture and re-roll knobs (section 2).

## 4. Free-for-all posture: what differs

From tick 0 after 16:02 UTC today (clock switch), or after a foreign death. Practice knobs (opening gate,
attack-on-sight, near-only loot, drop-when-scratched) are off; the mixture changes only salts and practice knobs, so
all 16 buckets play nearly the same final.
- **Quiet opening:** first 90 s, and then as long as more than 6 are alive (up to 300 s): aim alone does not make a
  mech hostile beyond 60 m unless it charges a laser; does not close in on a target above 30% (holds at most
  current range + 10 m, cap 190 m) and does not chase it out of sight (hides instead); advantage-based fights only
  within hold + 50 m; does not fight a laser carrier without its own laser unless the kill is within 2.5 s; skips
  loot within 120 m of a mech seen in the last 8 s, and loot near heard noises (150 m, far band 190 m) unless it is a
  laser within 70 m; with nothing to do it moves to the spot farthest from known mechs and noises (rings 30-90 m).
- **Patient endgame:** from the first death until two remain, it only fights mechs that hit it in the last 4 s,
  hostile mechs within 70 m, and mechs under 30% within 130 m while it is above 50%. Before the first death it also
  third-parties a "busy" mech within 180 m if not rated more than 1.6x stronger, no other hostile is near and it is
  above 60%.
- **Strength avoidance:** a mech within 300 m rated more than 1.5x its strength (health x damage at 90 m against its
  own) is avoided inside 90 m or when it has a line within 220 m; loot within 100 m of it (or within 150 m and 15 m
  nearer to it than we are) is dropped, and loot in its view within 260 m too. While more than 6 are alive and not quiet, loot within 90 m of any mech rated
  0.9x or more is skipped.
- Cover prefers spots not closer to any hostile; evades an unseen laser sniper even with a visible target.
- **Laser caution on:** steps that expose it to a laser that can fire within 0.85 s cost about 400; it lurks at cover
  edges; it will not start its own charge while its target charges.
- Loot at 0.6 per metre (cube ~183 m, crate ~175 m, drone ~283 m, laser ~450 m); pile bonus +30 per extra cube within
  14 m (up to 6); explores unseen ground while it has no laser and no danger within 110 m; climbs roofs for weapons
  without a laser unless threatened; walks to heard deaths (near band 35 m out, value 175; mid band 105 m, 170;
  exact spot when a mech was seen there, 120 + 40 per cube, up to 4), gives up after 45 s.
- Supply drops as a priority move only under 60% health, no strong mech near, landed, waited 10 s unless under 50%,
  not held, no other mech within 40 m; otherwise a drop is an ordinary loot objective (value 170, 60 if held).
- Watchdogs: loot with no progress for 12-14 s is ignored 45-60 s; 14 s of dithering inside 12 m triggers a 9 s break
  to a point 90 m away (toward the zone centre, away from strong mechs).
- Same aiming, dodging, zone and retreat (35% -> 80%) as practice.

### 5.2 Final-only (no practice effect)

Quiet opening (90 s / more than 6 alive / 300 s cap) with no-aim-hostility, no-close, no-chase, laser-flee and
noise avoidance; patient endgame from the first death; busy-mech third-party attacks; strength avoidance at 1.5x
with 90 / 220 m distances; keep-away at 0.9x; loot hidden from strong mechs; safer cover; sniper evasion; final drop
rule; grab; death sites; exploration; roof weapons; watchdog and break; pile bonus; noise map.

### 5.3 What moved the score

- **5.94 -> 6.58 (+31 kills): the mixture (P10), essentially alone.** A strip of comments and a line diff between
  the 16:00 lot tip (`631000e`) and `4392c25` shows every other change gated to the final posture, plus the two
  final detectors and the jitter knob. Size check with our own numbers: re-draw spread of a fixed bot is sd 0.17
  (8.3 kills over 48 matches), so about 2.1 kills per bucket of 3 matches; picking the best of 3-4 variants per
  bucket with exact knowledge gives +28 to +35 kills over 16 buckets. Their gain sits right there.
- **5.60 -> 5.94 (+16 kills):** P1-P7 (most plausibly the drop rule P7, the wider and lower attack gate P2 and the
  grab P5), but note that 2696's visible best is also the best of many pinned salts (about 20 salt variants of this
  profile were pinned Sat 11:08-16:00). Best-of-20 draws alone is worth about +1.9 sd = +0.3, so the true mean of the reference
  bot may be near 5.6-5.7, not 5.94.

## 6. Our best build (`variants6/FNV_s1`, SELECT in `bot/lib/params.js`) against theirs

Our build as resolved: no opening gate (fightEarly on turns the farm-first opening off), 20 s guard, any mech
within our band + 40 m (225 m with a laser) is a candidate after 20 s at any health, unengaged attack at 70% or more
before the first foreign death, seek on, laser band 125-185 m (hold 150), gun-only 55-95 m, lightning rush 28 m,
never leave a fight in SQUAD (loseCover never), heal only out of contact under 55% (exit 70%), DROP below FIGHT and
HEAL, laser-charge cover step on in SQUAD, crates and drones only at 90% or more until 210 s, cube grabs up to 70 m
mid-fight, kill cubes up to 200 m. Score 5.38 (best of 5 salts; mean 5.11, sd 0.17).

### 6.1 Ranked gaps (likely effect on the practice score)

| Rank | Behaviour | Theirs | Ours | Likely effect | Notes |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Per-slot variant mixture tuned on the fixed 48 matches** | 16 buckets (hash of hello seed + slot), 25 variants, searched with masks and 4-bucket swaps; exact because the scorer is deterministic and buckets add up | whole-build salt redraws only (5 draws) | **+0.3 to +0.8** (largest available) | Practice-only, zero expected value in the final. Needs frozen code (any code change reshuffles every bucket; they re-pin the reference on each build). Costs: 16 submissions for an exact 2-variant design, about 4 per new variant with group swaps; at 4 per hour that is most of today's slots. It is benchmark overfitting; organisers "verify the top results"; owner's call. |
| 2 | **Supply drop as a second life** | any drop within 200 m as soon as below 100%, priority over fighting, no contest check, no health margin; stand on it 4 s for full repair + 3 cubes | DROP only when no target, not healing, not losing; health margin; skip if any mech within 60 m; landed drops only within 70 m | likely +0.1 to +0.4 | Their reference kept it in every pin for 15 h of salt-controlled testing. Our "dropLife" idea in the log is the same thing. Biggest real-play gap. |
| 3 | **Clock-based final switch** (enabler) | final posture from tick 0 after 16:02 UTC; also ready-gap over 400 ms | SQUAD until 3 foreign deaths (median 18 s) | indirect: frees every practice-only change from the "final-safe" constraint | Risk: any practice re-scoring after the cutoff (verification) would replay the final posture and not reproduce the score. Ready-gap threshold would need our own measurement. |

| 5 | Opening gate per slot, not global | 75 s / 10-cube gate in 12 buckets, "never start a fight" in 4 | global fightEarly (farm-first lost 4.60 vs 4.98, one draw each, older code) | via rank 1 | The 4 passive buckets say a passive variant wins some slots; include it as a mixture variant rather than a global rule. |

and lead are of the same class.

## 7. Caveats

- Which of the six 02:18-02:19 pins scored 6.58 is not certain; push times were unavailable.
- The mixture reading assumes the bucket is effectively per slot and fixed across the 48 practice matches (rules
  L7/L11 and the scorer's determinism, both supported by our own resubmissions scoring identically).
- Gains in 5.3 and 6.1 are arithmetic on our measured re-draw spread, not measurements of their bot.
- Their final play is read from code only.
